born.why: The code now distinguishes between items that are merely "not harmful" (worst delta > 0) and those that are "beneficial" (best gain < -5). It avoids any item type where the worst recorded outcome increased n1 by more than 10, preventing catastrophic spikes. It only recommends/approaches items with a history of significantly reducing n1, ensuring the agent prioritizes survival-enhancing interactions over neutral or risky ones.

The code prioritizes survival by avoiding risky actions when n1 is high, and only engages with items that have a proven history of reducing n1 (health gain) for that specific kind, defaulting to the safest option otherwise.
It avoids items with a history of causing large n1 spikes (delta > 10) and prioritizes those that reduce n1, falling back to a safe option 'a4' when danger is high or the default choice is risky.

The agent currently blindly follows the default choice `x.n5`, which leads to high-risk items (like k=344 and k=110) that spike `n1` dangerously. By adding a check for high `n1` levels, the agent will refuse risky actions when close to death, prioritizing survival over immediate gains, while continuing to take safe, low-risk actions (like k=321) when healthy.

The code improves decision-making by calculating a "score" (health gain per cost) from historical data for the specific item kind, preferring options that historically lowered n1 efficiently, while adding a critical safety check for high n1 states to prevent death.
